question: Which of these schemes is implemented to promote organic farming?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) is a sub-component of the Soil Health Management (SHM) scheme under the National Mission of Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA).
 
• The scheme was launched in 2015 to promote organic farming and improve soil health by reducing the dependence on chemical fertilizers and pesticides.
 
• PKVY helps farmers adopt organic farming practices such as the use of bio-fertilizers, vermicomposting, and traditional techniques to improve crop productivity sustainably.
 
• Under the scheme, farmers are incentivized to form clusters of 20 hectares to take up organic farming collectively, thereby reducing input costs and improving yields.
 
• The scheme also focuses on creating market linkages for organic produce, promoting Participatory Guarantee Systems (PGS), and assisting farmers in getting organic certification.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY)**

 
 
• PM-KMY is a pension scheme introduced in 2019 for small and marginal farmers.
 
• Farmers aged between 18 and 40 years can enroll in this scheme, contributing a small monthly premium based on their age.
 
• On attaining the age of 60, enrolled farmers receive a minimum fixed pension of Rs. 3,000 per month.
 
• The scheme aims to provide social security to farmers after their retirement.
 
 
 
• **Soil Health Card Scheme (SHC)**
 
 
• The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2015 to promote soil testing and balanced use of fertilizers.
 
• Under this scheme, farmers receive soil health cards containing detailed information about the nutrient content of their soil.
 
• The cards provide recommendations on the type and quantity of fertilizers required to improve soil health and crop productivity.
 
• The scheme aims to reduce overuse of fertilizers, increase crop yields, and improve soil fertility.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA)**
 
 
• ATMA is a central sector scheme launched in 2005 as part of the National Mission on Agricultural Extension and Technology (NMAET).
 
• It aims to strengthen extension services by integrating research and extension activities at the district level.
 
• ATMA focuses on capacity-building, training, and dissemination of technology to farmers through Farmer Field Schools (FFS) and demonstrations.
 
• The scheme emphasizes participatory and bottom-up planning for agricultural development.
